doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Ray Charles and the shelved album
title: Aside about Tony Gumina and the album cover
summary: A brief aside on Tony Gumina, then the cover with a male model that did not bother him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah. So you’re a happy guy. So here comes the first, in your mind . . .
Yes.
. . . great Jimmy Scott album that expresses your heart and your soul and your artistry . . .
Yes, right.
. . . in a way that makes you happy . . .
Right.
. . . not only because you’ve got him playing behind you. You’ve got these beautiful orchestrations.
Right. And I’ve got to tell you something about that.
Please. We want to hear it.
I got to tell.
I want to hear it.
Listen. What’s his name? Tony or something?
Tony Gumina. The cat who lives down the street here? In Vegas?
Has he been to see you?
Yeah. I know Tony well.
You know the program he’s after.
Yeah.
Good. Okay. I just wanted to make sure . . .
I’m behind it.
. . . you knew, because . . .
No. I talk to him all the time. No, Tony wants to help you, and I want to help Tony help you, and blah blah.

Anyway, getting back to the – right, please God – getting back to the thing about – right – so, the album’s done. Ray let you be need to be and who you are. The orchestrations are beautiful. The tunes are all the songs that are of your heart songs.
Yes. Of my heart.

Now, the first that happens, that a cover of the album comes out, and there’s not your picture on it. There’s a male model on the cover. What was your reaction when the album came out and your picture wasn’t on it. Did that . . . ?
Oh that. He . . .
Joe Adams.
He was a no-time tap dancer.
Oh, the model.
The man that – yeah, that was on that album.
That’s interesting.
And the girl – I don’t know who the girl was.
She was probably a model too.
Probably a model or [?].
Did that hurt you?
Huh?
Did that hurt you, when you saw a Jimmy Scott album?
No.
So you didn’t care.
No. I was so glad that Ray was playing with me. I never thought of those things, about who was who.
